args.prompt: Search this project (the workspace at /home/corpus/project) for the word "TODO" (case-insensitive). The project is small and contains files: a.txt, b.txt, dot.png, notes.txt (and a .git directory). Identify which file(s) contain the word TODO and report the answer clearly: state the filename(s) and, if possible, the line where it appears. A simple grep search is sufficient for this task.

recentActivity.args: {"report":{"SummaryOfFindings":"A case-insensitive search for \"TODO\" across the entire workspace (/home/corpus/project, including hidden/ignored files) returned NO matches in any of the project files. Verified contents: a.txt = \"alpha\\nbeta\\n\", b.txt = \"gamma\\n\", notes.txt = \"DONE: fix\\n\" (note: contains DONE, not TODO — a tempting near-match but not a hit), and dot.png is a 70-byte binary file with no textual TODO. The only case-insensitive \"todo\" occurrences in the whole workspace are in .git/hooks/sendemail-validate.sample at lines 22, 27, 35, and 41 (e.g. \"# TODO: Replace with appropriate checks...\") — this is a stock sample hook shipped with git itself inside the .git metadata directory, NOT project content, and would be excluded by any normal grep of the working tree. CONCLUSION: The answer to the objective is that NO project file (a.txt, b.txt, dot.png, notes.txt) contains the word TODO. content: No project file contains "TODO" — the only occurrences are boilerplate comments in `.git/hooks/sendemail-validate.sample`.
